65-163.r: Jonas Salk (American virologist, New York) → discovered and developed the first successful polio vaccine.

65-164.r: Arber and Smith → restriction endonucleases; Feldmann → transgenic plants with Agrobacterium T-DNA; Mullis → polymerase chain reaction (PCR); Temin and Baltimore → reverse transcriptase.

65-165.r: All correct: Francis Collins → human genome mapping (led Human Genome Project); Sergey Brin → Google (with Larry Page); Jimmy Wales → Wikipedia.

65-166.r: Cycle of erosion (geographical cycle of landscape development) → William Morris Davis.

65-167.r: Auxanometer → instrument to measure the rate of growth in plants.
65-167.h: Auxano = to grow (like auxin, the growth hormone).

65-168.r: Mestizo → person of mixed European and Indigenous American (Indian) ancestry in Latin America (from Latin 'mixticius' = mixed).

65-169.r: Age of most ancient mountain rocks → uranium-lead (U-Pb) method; carbon-14 (radiocarbon) dating → age of fossils and organic material.

65-171.r: Age of a tree → count of annual (growth) rings in its stem; one ring per year.

65-172.r: Clay retains most water (A true) because its fine particles leave many SMALL pore spaces, not large ones (R false).

65-173.r: Alkaline soils → improved by adding gypsum (also leaching, subsurface drainage, crop rotation).

65-174.r: Huge fall in butterflies → pollination of some plants suffers; wasps, spiders, birds that eat them decline (1, 3); no rise in fungal infections.

65-175.r: World's most problematic aquatic weed → Eichhornia (water hyacinth), 'Terror of Bengal'; spreads fast and chokes water bodies.

65-176.r: Red tides → blooms of pigmented dinoflagellates/algae colouring estuary and coastal water (often red); may release toxins or use up oxygen.

65-177.r: Only 2 true: a chameleon can look ahead with one eye and behind with the other. Spirogyra is a freshwater green alga ('pond silk'), not found in oceans.

65-178.r: Mycorrhiza (fungus–plant root symbiosis) → helps plants resist drought, enlarge absorptive area, tolerate pH extremes and resist disease (all three).

65-179.r: Biorock technology → restoring damaged coral reefs (also seagrass, mangroves); invented 1976 by Wolf Hilbertz.

65-180.r: Phytotron → enclosed research greenhouse to grow plants under controlled conditions (plant-environment studies).

65-181.r: Polyhouse (polytunnel of polyethylene) → for growing plants; protects crops from bright sun, hail and storms.

65-182.r: Papaya, pineapple and guava (New World fruits) → all three brought to India by the Portuguese in the 16th-17th centuries (papaya about 1611 AD).

65-183.r: Linen → flax plant; Coir → coconut plant; Mohair → Angora goat; Down → feathers of ducks and geese.

65-184.r: Angora wool → Angora rabbit (downy coat); mohair comes from the Angora goat.
65-184.t: Angora wool = rabbit; mohair = Angora goat.

65-187.r: Light emitted by living organisms (marine animals, insects) → bioluminescence: chemical reaction of luciferin with luciferase or photoprotein.

65-188.r: Green Revolution high-yielding seeds → needed more fertilizer and more water.

65-189.r: Green Revolution → food grains; White → milk and milk products; Yellow → oilseeds; Blue → fish and aquaculture.

65-190.r: Principal crop of the Green Revolution → Mexican wheat.

65-191.r: Dapog method of rice nursery → developed in the Philippines; about 25 to 30 m² raises seedlings for one hectare.

65-192.r: First dwarf rice variety developed in India → Jaya.
65-192.t: IR-8 came from IRRI (option a); Jaya was India's own.

65-193.r: Mosquito control fish → Gambusia (family Poeciliidae, 3-5 cm), released in ponds and wells to eat mosquito larvae and eggs.

65-195.r: Active acquired immunity → body's own production of antibodies (immunoglobulins) by B lymphocytes (B cells).

65-196.r: Science and Technology Policy 2003 (January 3, 2003, 90th Science Congress, Bengaluru) → all four: resource use, innovative technologies, natural-hazard mitigation, intellectual property.

65-197.r: First country to ban sale of tobacco and its products → Bhutan (December 2004).

65-198.r: Planet possibly suitable for life → Mars (near and similar to Earth; search for habitability and organic compounds continues).

65-199.r: Development of natural systems → described as a self-sustained process of the systems.

65-200.r: TIVA, from Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology → claimed to cut flower drop in pulses. The book gives no single answer (*).
65-200.c: The book's explanation defines TIVA as total intravenous anaesthesia, which has nothing to do with pulses; it does not settle the question.

65-201.r: Justified true belief → knowledge (traditional tripartite 'JTB' analysis of knowledge).

65-202.r: Both true: scientific investigation depends on commitment to practical ideals; honesty is particularly important in science.

65-203.r: Knowledge gained at school (facts, ideas, meanings, concepts) → semantic memory, a part of long-term memory.

65-204.r: Mental activity in the brain while processing, organising and communicating information → thinking.
